title: Establish SDK failsafe profiles, resumable-stream contracts, and error-class mapping
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Define and implement a cross-language (Python, TypeScript, Go) set of "failsafe" retry/backoff profiles, a resumable-stream contract (resume token semantics and schema), and an explicit mapping from platform+network errors to SDK-level retry categories. This ticket captures design decisions, compatibility constraints, rollout plan, and sample usage patterns for each SDK.

Background: Teams keep re-implementing similar heuristics for retries, backoff, and streaming resume logic across languages. That leads to inconsistent behavior, customer confusion when switching runtimes, and brittle heuristic forks. We need a single canonical set of defaults (P99 / P50 latency-targeted options), a small surface for opt-in/customization, and a contract for resumable streams so apps can safely persist resume tokens across SDK updates.

Deliverables:
- Spec document describing three failsafe profiles (low-latency, balanced, cost-optimized) with numeric defaults for initial delay, multiplier, jitter, max attempts, and total time cap.
- Resumable-stream contract: canonical resume token format (versioned opaque base64 JSON with timestamp, request-hash, byte-offset), validation rules, and migration story for older token shapes.
- Retryable error taxonomy: list mapping HTTP codes, gRPC codes, and known transient internal errors to categories: retryable-immediately, retry-with-backoff, non-retryable, idempotency-dependent.
- Cross-SDK API surfaces: small ergonomic helpers for common patterns (with_failsafe_profile, .resume_from(token), IdempotencyKey helpers) with examples for Python/TS/Go.
- Telemetry plan: metric labels and traces to capture profile name, attempt count, backoff type, resume-token-validity, and final outcome.
- Tests: unit tests across simulated transient errors, integration tests with the serving runtime (fault injection), and backwards-compat validation of resumed tokens.

Design notes / constraints:
- Defaults must be conservative for hosted: balanced profile default attempts = 4, initial_delay=50ms, multiplier=2.0, jitter=0.2, total_time_cap=8s. Low-latency uses initial=10ms, attempts=3, cap=2s. Cost-optimized uses initial=200ms, attempts=6, cap=20s. Values are proposals and will be validated by perf tests.
- Resume token must be forward-compatible. Token schema: {"v":1, "h":<sha256hex>, "o":<offset>, "t":<iso8601>} encoded base64url. SDKs must accept tokens with unknown future fields but reject malformed ones.
- Idempotency key guidance: prefer user-supplied idempotency keys for bearing stateful operations; SDK will auto-generate when caller omits it for safe-by-default endpoints. Auto-generated keys include a short TTL and are logged in telemetry with hashing to avoid PII.
- Error taxonomy will map server-side transient codes (HTTP 429, 503, gRPC UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) to retry-with-backoff. Permanent errors (4xx other than 429) map to non-retryable. Edge cases where idempotency matters (e.g., HTTP 500 on operation with no idempotency key) are classified as idempotency-dependent and surfaced to callers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cross-SDK spec reviewed and approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and Runtime team.
- Implementation libraries expose with_failsafe_profile and resume helpers with identical semantics in all three SDKs.
- Integration tests demonstrate resumed streaming success across a simulated restart and that resume token from SDK vX can be accepted by SDK vX+1.
- Telemetry metrics emitted and visible in Console prototype dashboards for experiments.

Rollout plan:
1) Finalize spec and land design doc (Confluence) — owner Aisha.
2) Implement feature-flagged support in Python and TypeScript SDKs; integration test harness with serving runtime fault-injection — owner Marcus.
3) Dogfood internally with two teams and capture telemetry for one week.
4) Implement Go SDK parity and remove feature flags if no major regressions.

Compatibility & migration:
- Provide a compatibility shim for older SDKs where server can accept older token formats; server will translate to canonical v1 when possible.
- Document changes and offer a migration script for persisted tokens older than v1.

Open questions:
- Should auto-generated idempotency keys be stable across retries inside a single logical operation boundary (yes) and how long should their TTL be (proposal 1 hour)?
- Do we expose jitter as a configurable knob or keep it fixed behind profiles? (proposal: fixed per-profile, advanced API for custom backoff).
- Does resume token include model hash or request hash? Current draft includes request-hash; runtime team to confirm feasibility.
